subtitle: When the Great Gun Fell Silent

panels.shot: epic wide shot from the battlements looking down over Bijapur's walls and the Malik-i-Maidan cannon toward the dust cloud of the approaching Mughal host
panels.action: Aurangzeb and Sikandar Adil Shah stand apart on the massive Bijapur ramparts near the dark bulk of the Malik-i-Maidan gun, each gazing in opposite directions as an immense Mughal army advances across the dry Deccan plain below.

dialogue.text: In 1685, under the silent gaze of the Malik-i-Maidan at Bijapur, Aurangzeb and Sikandar Adil Shah faced a siege that would destroy a kingdom but leave the Deccan war forever unfinished.

i18n.hi: १६८५ में, बीजापुर के मलिक-ए-मैदान की खामोश नजरों तले, औरंगज़ेब और सिकंदर आदिल शाह ऐसी घेराबंदी में फंसे जो एक सल्तनत मिटाएगी, पर दक्खन की जंग अधूरी ही छोड़ेगी।

panels.shot: slow push-in over a parchment map of the Deccan, Mughal frontier lines creeping southward toward Bijapur
panels.action: A worn hand-drawn map of the Deccan lies on a wooden table, showing the long Mughal frontier pressing down toward Bijapur, Golconda and Maratha-held hill forts, with small tokens marking armies and supply routes.

dialogue.text: For half a century, the Mughal frontier had crept into the Deccan, swallowing sultanates and hill forts, yet the southern plateau remained a maze of enemies, empty treasuries and burning supply lines.

i18n.hi: पचास बरस तक मुगल सरहदें दक्खन में रेंगती बढ़ीं, सल्तनतें और किलों को निगलती रहीं, पर दक्षिण का पठार अब भी दुश्मनों, खाली ख़ज़ानों और जली हुई रसद-लाइनों की भूलभुलैया बना रहा।

panels.shot: medium profile of Aurangzeb in a campaign tent, lamplight on his face as he considers letters from the Deccan
panels.action: Aurangzeb sits upright on a low campaign seat in a dim tent, white beard neatly trimmed, eyes sharp, as he studies a pile of Deccan dispatches laid beside a small globe and prayer beads.

dialogue.text: By the 1680s, Aurangzeb, now in his seventies, ruled almost all Hindustan, yet his letters speak of Deccan princes who defied him, Maratha raids and the need to break Bijapur before all else.

i18n.hi: १६८० के दशक तक, सत्तर पार का औरंगज़ेब लगभग सारे हिंदुस्तान पर बैठा था, पर उसके खतें दक्खनी रियासतों की सानेहधानी, मराठा धावों और सबसे पहले बीजापुर तोड़ने की ज़िद से भरे थे।

panels.shot: wide shot in the Bijapur durbar, low-angle on young Sikandar Adil Shah on the throne amid anxious nobles
panels.action: In the grand audience hall of Bijapur, the youthful Sikandar Adil Shah sits on an ornate throne, his face tense, while turbaned amirs argue and gesture around him beneath high carved arches.

dialogue.text: In Bijapur, the Adil Shahi throne had passed to the young Sikandar, heir to a two-century-old sultanate now weakened by faction, empty granaries and the looming shadow of Mughal power.

i18n.hi: बीजापुर में दो सौ बरस पुरानी आदिलशाही गद्दी अब नौजवान सिकंदर के हाथ थी, ऐसी सल्तनत का वारिस जो गुटबाज़ी, खाली कोठारों और मुगल साये से भीतर ही भीतर खोखली हो चुकी थी।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of the Malik-i-Maidan cannon on the ramparts at dusk, tiny soldiers around it
panels.action: The colossal bronze barrel of the Malik-i-Maidan cannon dominates the rampart, its dark muzzle directed over the moat and plain, as small Bijapuri gunners stand near it, dwarfed by its size in the fading light.

dialogue.text: On those walls sat the Malik-i-Maidan, the ‘Lord of the Plain’, a giant gun cast in an earlier age, now more symbol than weapon, but to Bijapur it still embodied the hope of holding back an empire.

i18n.hi: उन्हीं दीवारों पर बैठा था मलिक-ए-मैदान, ‘मैदान का मालिक’, पुरानी सदियों में ढली विशाल तोप, अब हथियार से ज्यादा निशान, पर बीजापुर के लिए अभी भी एक ऐसे सहारे की उम्मीद, जो साम्राज्य की लहर रोक दे।

panels.shot: broad panoramic shot of the Mughal army columns marching toward Bijapur under a harsh sun
panels.action: Long columns of Mughal infantry, cavalry and ox-drawn artillery roll across the parched Deccan, banners fluttering and dust rising, as officers ride along the flanks pointing toward the distant dark line of Bijapur's walls.

dialogue.text: In 1685, Aurangzeb sent his generals with great hosts and heavy guns toward Bijapur, ordering them to ring it with trenches, batteries and watchtowers until the Adil Shahi capital could neither breathe nor trade.

i18n.hi: १६८५ में औरंगज़ेब ने भारी फौजों और तोपखाने के साथ अपने सरदारों को बीजापुर पर चढ़ा दिया, हुक्म दिया कि खाइयों, बैटरियों और मीनारों की ऐसी घेराबंदी करो कि आदिलशाही राजधानी न सांस ले सके, न सौदा।

panels.shot: high-angle shot showing Bijapur’s massive walls, moat and outworks facing Mughal siege lines in the distance
panels.action: From above, the thick polygonal walls and wide moat of Bijapur surround the crowded city, while beyond them Mughal siege lines slowly take shape, zig-zagging trenches creeping closer and gun platforms rising from bare earth.

dialogue.text: Maasir-i-Alamgiri speaks of strong walls, deep ditches and stubborn defenders; the first Mughal attack lines stalled, their guns thundering but their trenches checked by stone, water and counter-fire.

i18n.hi: ‘मासिर-ए-आलमगिरी’ मजबूत दीवारों, गहरी खाइयों और अड़ियल रक्षकों का ज़िक्र करता है; पहला मुगल हमला अटक गया, तोपें गरजीं पर उनकी खाइयाँ पत्थर, पानी और जवाबी गोली से थम गईं।

panels.shot: close shot of Sikandar on the ramparts at night, lit by torches, listening to distant gunfire
panels.action: Sikandar Adil Shah stands wrapped in a cloak on the night rampart, torchlight flickering on his face as he peers into the darkness beyond the moat, where flashes from Mughal guns light the horizon.

dialogue.speaker: aurangzeb_and_sikandar_adil_shah
dialogue.text: We hold, so long as grain holds.

i18n.hi: हम तब तक टिके हैं, जब तक अनाज टिके।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of Maratha horsemen raiding a Mughal supply convoy in the countryside
panels.action: Fast-moving Maratha cavalry sweep down on a long line of Mughal pack animals in the scrubland, drivers scattering as the raiders seize loads and drive off cattle, distant hills and smoke on the horizon behind them.

dialogue.text: While the siege tightened, Bhimsen records another war, out of sight of the walls: Maratha horse under Sambhaji striking caravans, burning depots and turning the Mughal lifeline in the Deccan into a path of hunger.

i18n.hi: घेरा कसता गया, और भिमसेन दीवारों की आंखों से ओझल एक और जंग लिखता है: संभाजी के नेतृत्त्व में मराठा घुड़सवार काफिलों पर धावा बोलते, गोदाम जलाते और मुगल रसद-राह को भूख की डगर में बदल देते।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a Mughal camp kitchen, soldiers waiting with empty bowls, looking weary
panels.action: Inside a rough Mughal camp kitchen of mud and cloth, gaunt soldiers stand in line with wooden bowls as a cook scrapes the bottom of a pot, the smoke thin and the rations clearly meagre.

dialogue.text: Nuskha-i-Dilkusha speaks of long marches, short rations and men selling horses and arms to buy food, as disease crept through the besiegers’ tents even while they spent treasure and lives to choke Bijapur.

i18n.hi: ‘नुस्खा-ए-दिलकुशा’ लंबी यात्राओं, कम राशन, और उन सिपाहियों का हाल सुनाता है जो पेट भरने को घोड़े-बंदूक तक बेचते, जबकि बीमारी घेरने वालों के डेरे-डेरों में घुसती जाती और ख़ज़ाना व जानें बीजापुर का गला दबाने में झोंक दी जातीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Aurangzeb mounting a horse near the Narmada, army behind him, heading south
panels.action: Aurangzeb, in plain but regal campaign dress, mounts a horse with deliberate calm beside the Narmada bank, while behind him officers bow and the standards of the imperial camp begin to move southward.

dialogue.text: Reports of delay and failure reached the emperor; the chronicler notes his resolve as he chose to leave the northern capitals and ride south himself, turning his court into a moving camp for the Deccan war.

i18n.hi: देरी और नाकामी की खबरें बादशाह तक पहुंचीं; तारीख़नवीस लिखता है कि उसने उत्तरी राजधानियां छोड़ने और खुद दक्खन को रवाना होने का इरादा किया, दरबार को ही एक चलता-फिरता जंगी डेरा बना डाला।

panels.shot: grand wide shot of Aurangzeb’s arrival before Bijapur, banners and elephants facing the distant fort
panels.action: Aurangzeb’s royal pavilion is being raised on a ridge overlooking Bijapur, elephants kneeling and standards waving, as the emperor surveys the distant fort whose walls and towers stand stubborn against the sky.

dialogue.text: When Aurangzeb reached Bijapur in 1686, Mughal lines already ringed the city; Maasir-i-Alamgiri credits his presence, his order to press the trenches closer and concentrate guns, with reviving a weary siege.

i18n.hi: १६८६ में जब औरंगज़ेब बीजापुर पहुंचा, मुगल रेखाएं शहर को पहले ही जकड़े थीं; ‘मासिर-ए-आलमगिरी’ उसके पहुंचने, खाइयां और सटा देने और तोपों को जुटाने के हुक्म को थकी घेराबंदी को फिर जान देने का कारण मानता है।

panels.shot: low-angle along the trench line, Mughal sappers creeping toward the walls under cover of mantlets
panels.action: Mughal sappers crouch in narrow trenches cut across dry earth, pushing heavy wooden shields as they inch toward Bijapur’s wall, while behind them artillery crews load a great gun aimed at a battered bastion.

dialogue.text: Day by day, trenches inched closer, batteries shifted, bastions cracked; the defenders answered with counter-mines and shot, but each night the sappers returned, driven by imperial orders and the promise of reward.

i18n.hi: दिन-ब-दिन खाइयां रेंग कर पास आईं, बैटरियां बदलीं, बुर्ज चटके; रक्षक भी सुरंगें खोद कर, गोले दाग कर जवाब देते रहे, पर हर रात बादशाही हुक्म और इनाम के लालच से चलती ज़ंजीर-खुदाई फिर लौट आती।

panels.shot: close-up of the Malik-i-Maidan cannon’s muzzle, a thin crack visible, gunners resting beside it
panels.action: The dark bronze muzzle of the Malik-i-Maidan fills the frame, its surface worn and faintly cracked, as tired Bijapuri gunners sit beside it in the heat, eyes hollow, looking across at the distant Mughal lines.

dialogue.text: The great Malik-i-Maidan itself loomed over the plain, but sources suggest it saw little decisive use; in this siege, prestige guns could not feed men or conjure allies, and walls could not march to break the encirclement.

i18n.hi: महान मलिक-ए-मैदान सारा मैदान ढके खड़ा था, पर तारीखें मानती हैं कि उसका असली इस्तेमाल कम ही हुआ; इस घेराबंदी में शाने-दिखाऊ तोपें न आदमी को खाना दे सकीं, न साथी जादू से बुला सकीं, और दीवारें चलकर घेरा तोड़ नहीं सकती थीं।

panels.shot: somber indoor shot in Bijapur’s council chamber, nobles arguing while a map of the city lies open
panels.action: Inside a dim chamber, Sikandar sits at a low table with a map of the city before him, while his nobles argue, some pointing out toward the walls, others toward imagined routes of escape, their faces lined with exhaustion.

dialogue.speaker: aurangzeb_and_sikandar_adil_shah
dialogue.text: If the city starves, what remains of a throne?

i18n.hi: अगर शहर भूखा मर जाए, तो गद्दी में क्या बचता है?

panels.shot: intense interior shot of Aurangzeb in his tent, a messenger kneeling with a sealed letter
panels.action: A Bijapuri envoy kneels in Aurangzeb’s tent, holding out a sealed letter with trembling hands, while the emperor listens impassively, a small writing desk and copies of the Quran arranged carefully beside him.

dialogue.text: After months of assault, hunger and mounting losses, the sources describe parleys and envoys; Sikandar’s court, divided and desperate, began to seek terms with a ruler who would demand submission, not alliance.

i18n.hi: महीनों की मारकाट, भूख और बढ़ती जान-माल की हानि के बाद, हवाले कहानियां सुनाते हैं मुलाक़ातों और वफ्दों की; सिकंदर का दरबार, बिखरा और बेसहारा, ऐसे बादशाह से सुलह टटोलने लगा जो दोस्ती नहीं, सर झुकाने की मांग करेगा।

panels.shot: solemn wide shot of Sikandar leaving the fort gate with a small retinue, Mughal lines in the distance
panels.action: Sikandar Adil Shah rides out from the main gate of Bijapur, dressed plainly but royally, accompanied by a small retinue, as Mughal cavalry watch from afar and the fortress looms heavy behind him.

dialogue.text: In late 1686, Sikandar surrendered; chroniclers describe him leaving his battered capital to present himself before Aurangzeb, the last Adil Shahi sultan walking out from the walls his ancestors had raised.

i18n.hi: १६८६ के आखिर में सिकंदर ने हथियार डाल दिए; तारीख़नवीस लिखते हैं कि वह अपनी उजड़ी राजधानी से निकलकर औरंगज़ेब के सामने जा खड़ा हुआ, आख़िरी आदिलशाही सुल्तान, उन दीवारों से बाहर निकलते हुए जिन्हें उसके बाप-दादाओं ने खड़ा किया था।

panels.shot: formal mid-shot in the Mughal camp, Sikandar standing before Aurangzeb seated on a simple throne
panels.action: Inside the Mughal camp pavilion, Aurangzeb sits on a simple raised seat, austere and composed, while Sikandar stands before him with folded hands, head slightly bowed, Mughal officers watching in measured silence.

dialogue.text: Maasir-i-Alamgiri relates that Aurangzeb received Sikandar with a mix of firmness and formality, sending him into honorable confinement while Bijapur’s officers were sorted, rewarded, punished or absorbed into the empire.

i18n.hi: ‘मासिर-ए-आलमगिरी’ के मुताबिक औरंगज़ेब ने सिकंदर को सख्ती और तहज़ीब के मिले-जुले अंदाज़ में लिया, उसे इज़्ज़तदार क़ैद में भेजा, और बीजापुर के अफसरों को छांट कर किसी को इनाम, किसी को सज़ा, तो किसी को साम्राज्य में मिला लिया।

panels.shot: expansive aerial shot over Bijapur, Mughal standards flying above the fort, the city within looking worn
panels.action: From high above, Bijapur’s fortifications encircle a city of smoke-stained roofs and crowded streets, while new Mughal standards flutter from the bastions and small groups of soldiers move through the exhausted town.

dialogue.text: With Bijapur taken, the Adil Shahi sultanate vanished from the map; its lands and great guns became Mughal, but its people, forts and countryside now had to be fed, garrisoned and held amid continuing raids and resistance.

i18n.hi: बीजापुर गिरते ही आदिलशाही सल्तनत नक्शे से मिट गई; उसकी ज़मीनें और बड़ी तोपें तो मुगल हो गईं, पर उसके लोग, किले और देहात अब मुगल पेट से, मुगल फौज से और लगातार छापों व बगावत के बीच ही संभाले जाने थे।

panels.shot: melancholic wide shot of Maratha riders in the distance as Mughal troops rest near Bijapur’s walls
panels.action: Near the outer walls, weary Mughal soldiers rest by their stacked arms as, far in the hazy distance, a small band of Maratha horsemen watch from a ridge before turning away toward the hills.

dialogue.text: Richards and Sarkar note that the fall of Bijapur did not end the Deccan war; even as Aurangzeb added another province, Maratha bands still moved in the distance, waiting for the next convoy, the next weak point.

i18n.hi: रिचर्ड्स और सरकार लिखते हैं कि बीजापुर की हार से दक्खन की जंग खत्म नहीं हुई; औरंगज़ेब ने एक सूबा और जोड़ लिया, पर दूर-दूर तक मराठा टोली अभी भी अगली रसद, अगला कमजोर मोर्चा तलाशती घूमती रही।

panels.shot: quiet close-up of the Malik-i-Maidan now under a Mughal guard, the city stretching beyond
panels.action: The Malik-i-Maidan cannon rests silently on the rampart under a lone Mughal sentry, who leans on his spear and gazes over the city, the vast plain fading into the evening haze beyond.

dialogue.text: The Malik-i-Maidan, once the pride of Bijapur, now stood as a Mughal trophy, yet its silence whispered a sharper lesson: an empire can seize a gun and a capital, and still find its war and burdens only deepened.

i18n.hi: मलिक-ए-मैदान, जो कभी बीजापुर का फख्र था, अब मुगल निशानी बनकर खामोश खड़ा था, पर उसकी चुप्पी एक तेज सबक देती रही: साम्राज्य तोप और राजधानी तो छीन सकता है, पर जंग और बोझ फिर भी और गहरा ही हो सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: When the Great Gun Fell Silent
